newsitem.title: USA: US FERC sets Union Electric/CIPSCO merger hearing.
newsitem.headline: US FERC sets Union Electric/CIPSCO merger hearing.

text.p: In an order that raised a number of concerns, the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday called for a hearing on the proposed merger of Union Electric Co and Central Illinois Public Service Co, a subsidiary of CIPSCO Inc.

The commission directed an administrative law judge to schedule a hearing on the plan to merge the utilities into a registered holding company called Ameren Corp. An administrative judge is to issue an initial decision by April 30, 1997.

Commissioner James Hoecker said the order will use Federal Trade Commission and Justice Department merger guidelines, and he said the order indicated that "a generic coming to terms with merger policy is not far off."
"All the handwringing about how hopelessly divided this commission is about what the public interest calculus for mergers ought to be in the future is obviously bunk," Hoecker said.

While he said FERC should handle merger authorizations faster than it has in this case, Hoecker said, "If anyone thinks we're going to set up a section 203 drive-up window for handing out merger authorizations, they're sadly mistaken."
Other commissioners said FERC should do a better job in specifying information it wants to speed up the authorization process.
The commission raised a number of questions in the order, including whether ratepayers -- particularly customers of Central Illinois -- would be adequately protected.

It also said the utilities had not given enough justification for their proposed cost-savings plan and cost recovery mechanism, saying it appeared the utilities' shareholders would be risk-free, while ratepayers would bear costs and risks.

The commission order also said under the applicants' proposal there was a potential to avoid FERC's authority to review certain costs, and also said it will look into effects on geographic markets and transmission constraints.
